evidence: Spearman(enrichment, precision) = -0.900, p=0.037 across the 5 classes; ordering stable at all 5 global budgets (1e4..5e6 sites). Ranking classes by margin-key ENRICHMENT sends bytes to MyCar (precision 0.2084); ranking by PRECISION sends them to Lane (0.6852). 3.29x fewer flips bought per site spent. Enrichment is a ratio to the class's OWN base rate, so it reports how unusual the bin is for that class -- a statement about the class's baseline, not about what a byte buys. 8th independent confirmation of law.aggregate_cashing_dead, in a new coordinate.
protection_ref: Needs the admission rule: rank by PRECISION (flips bought per site spent), never by enrichment. Enrichment may enter only as a prior on which sites to inspect. No gate currently blocks an enrichment-ranked allocator.

evidence: Within-Lane enrichment 2.5x -- the WORST of five classes and effectively non-discriminative, on the class carrying 36.53% of all flips. Per-class enrichment spans 2.5x (Lane) to 389.0x (MyCar), a 156x spread; mg1's population 98.6x describes NO class (m88: a population statistic over a mixture spanning 85x in area is a statement about the majority member). Mechanism: Lane's area/perimeter is 1.407 px vs Movable 11.07 / Road 21.93 / MyCar 97.41 / Undrivable 176.20 -- a class with no confident interior gives a margin key nothing to contrast the fragile boundary against. Lane is not a rare-fragile-site problem (the regime the key is good at); base flip rate 0.269028 means it is uniformly broken.

Lane precision 0.6852 in margin bin [0,0.096) -- the HIGHEST of all five classes, 3.29x MyCar's 0.2084; top-ranked at every budget (72.4/70.8/66.3/59.4/29.8% at 1e4/1e5/5e5/1e6/5e6 sites). Corrects the standing reading that Lane is the hard class: Lane is the CHEAPEST class in which to buy a flip. What is hard about Lane is CHOOSING which Lane pixels (see cg1.margin_key.lane_no_discrimination), not affording them. Reach and discrimination are separate dimensions and disagree in sign here -- global recall at a 1e6 budget is near parity (Lane 60.1% vs Road 69.6%, MyCar 82.1%), because Lane's sites are low-margin in ABSOLUTE terms and so rank high globally.

Per-class base flip rates under the live cx1 vehicle span 502x: Lane 0.269028, Movable 0.053983, Road 0.005591, Undrivable 0.001279, MyCar 0.000536. d_seg is a uniform per-pixel mean (upstream/modules.py:112-113, verified at source) and so weights each of these identically by AREA -- Undrivable at 49.52% of the plane contributes 14.69% of flips while Lane at 0.59% of the plane contributes 36.53%. Any statistic computed as a population mean over this mixture is dominated by the large-area classes and is silent about Lane.
protection_ref: Structural property of the frozen scorer; cannot be protected against, only routed around by conditioning every population statistic on class before it is used as a key.
